newsitem.title: USA: NASA approves Mir spacewalk training for Foale.
newsitem.headline: NASA approves Mir spacewalk training for Foale.

text.p: NASA has cleared American astronaut Michael Foale to train for a risky internal spacewalk to restore some power to the ailing Mir space station, a senior official of the U.S. space agency said on Thursday.
"We have given the go to the Russians for Mike to begin the training," said Frank Culbertson, a veteran shuttle commander who heads NASA's joint missions with Russia.

The spacewalk, which had tentatively been scheduled for July 24, is likely to be delayed because of the station's latest problems, which resulted in a total loss of power overnight. Mir's commander Vasily Tsiblyev was ruled out of the repair because of an irregular heart beat.

During the spacewalk flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin, assisted by Foale, would open up the airless Spektr module, holed in the June 25 crash of a cargo ship, to restore some of the power lost in the collision.

Foale is to participate in two rehearsals of the repair once the station's current power problems are resolved. NASA and the Russian space authorities will then decide whether to go ahead with the spacewalk, Culbertson said.
Foale, a British-born astrophysicist who is a U.S. citizen, made a spacewalk from the space shuttle Discovery in February 1995 and has trained to use a Russian space suit.
